questions.question: Analyse history as a reenactment of the past experience.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse history as a reenactment of the past experience. / – British historian RG
  • Collingwood proposed the concept of ‘reenactment’ – He argued that history is not merely a collection
  • of facts or a chronological narrative, but a complex process of mental reconstruction or "reenactment" of
  • past thoughts and experiences –It is an intellectual reimagining the cognitive landscape of a particular
  • historical moment through contextual understanding and sophisticated hermeneutic approach to
  • historical sources - Here historians must imaginatively recreate the mental processes and perspectives of
  • historical actors to truly comprehend historical events.
questions.final_answer: historical actors to truly comprehend historical events

questions.question: Can objectivity be considered the most cherished value in scientific research within the field of History? Critically examine.
questions.solution_html:
• Can objectivity be considered the most cherished value in scientific research within the
  • field of History? Critically examine. / – Though a cherished goal, achieving
  • complete objectivity in historical writing is undoubtedly challenging – Positivist notion of
  • objectivity is difficult to attain in history - History, by its nature, is a subject that cannot be
  • unbiased, objective, or merely factual - The question of historical objectivity is closely linked
  • with value judgment – There are many factors limiting historical objectivity including; Personal
  • and group prejudice, conflicting historical interpretations, differences in philosophical views
  • value judgements and moral values, incomplete evidences etc… - Consultation of maximum
  • possible sources, loyalty to facts, kept chauvinistic tendencies away from historical analysis etc
  • may help in objective treatment of sources and reading - Certainly, true objectivity is not
  • attainable, but it is nonetheless a reasonable and desirable goal for historians to strive for.
questions.final_answer: attainable, but it is nonetheless a reasonable and desirable goal for historians to strive for
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Analyse the development of major social science disciplines.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the development of major social science disciplines. / - Social sciences
  • emerged as object-specific, subjective disciplines by internalizing the cognitive modes, logical
  • structures, and communication strategies of scientific knowledge - The process occurred in five
  • Western nations (UK, France, Germany, Italy, US) with branches becoming academic
  • disciplines in universities by the nineteenth century - Core Disciplines: History, Economics
  • Sociology, Political Science, and Anthropology were institutionalized, especially after WWI –
  • Disciplines linked to the State Needs: History provided historicity for nation-states, Economics
  • (from Political Economy) met administrative needs, Sociology helped governments manage the
  • labour movement, Anthropology emerged from colonialist expansion to study non-European
  • societies – Following the Second World War the State-centric disciplines like Sociology
  • Political Science, and Economics became dominant, marginalizing those focused on universal
  • values, like History.
questions.final_answer: values, like History
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Assess the impact of stereotypes about India constructed during colonial period.
questions.solution_html:
• Assess the impact of stereotypes about India constructed during colonial period.
  • – Romila Thapar discussed about how the stereotypes about India constructed by the
  • Colonial historiography later contributed to the historical sense – Stereotype of Indians are
  • ahistorical about their past catered to the needs of colonialism and still remain in the
  • foundations of social consciousness and political ideology - The notion of traditional Indian
  • society as an unchanging society and the use of the Orient vs. Occident stereotype used to
  • create an image of Indian society without subjective freedom, property, and commercial
  • transactions - The Aryan and non-Aryan binary imposed a racial categorization over Indian
  • society - Another stereotype, that Indians were more spiritual than others, negated the

  • disciplines in universities by the nineteenth century - Core Disciplines: History, Economics
  • Sociology, Political Science, and Anthropology were institutionalized, especially after WWI –
  • Disciplines linked to the State Needs: History provided historicity for nation-states, Economics
  • (from Political Economy) met administrative needs, Sociology helped governments manage the
  • labour movement, Anthropology emerged from colonialist expansion to study non-European
  • societies – Following the Second World War the State-centric disciplines like Sociology
  • Political Science, and Economics became dominant, marginalizing those focused on universal
  • values, like History.
questions.final_answer: values, like History

questions.question: Assess the impact of stereotypes about India constructed during colonial period.
questions.solution_html:
• Assess the impact of stereotypes about India constructed during colonial period.
  • – Romila Thapar discussed about how the stereotypes about India constructed by the
  • Colonial historiography later contributed to the historical sense – Stereotype of Indians are
  • ahistorical about their past catered to the needs of colonialism and still remain in the
  • foundations of social consciousness and political ideology - The notion of traditional Indian
  • society as an unchanging society and the use of the Orient vs. Occident stereotype used to
  • create an image of Indian society without subjective freedom, property, and commercial
  • transactions - The Aryan and non-Aryan binary imposed a racial categorization over Indian
  • society - Another stereotype, that Indians were more spiritual than others, negated the
  • materialist outlook Indians shared and even today Indian society treated as an abode of
  • spirituality – Stereotype of separate nationhood on the basis of religion used to legitimize two
  • nation theory by communalists and used to spread communal divisiveness even today.
questions.final_answer: nation theory by communalists and used to spread communal divisiveness even today
